original_title: Fallout: New Vegas director Josh Sawyer reveals his optimal outcome for the Mojave Wasteland
summary_en: Josh Sawyer, the visionary director behind Fallout: New Vegas, has shared his personal ideal outcome for the Mojave Wasteland. Despite the game's multiple endings, Sawyer believes true 'optimal' satisfaction remains elusive in the harsh post-apocalyptic setting.
ai_analysis: This deep dive into Josh Sawyer's preferred Fallout: New Vegas ending offers a fascinating glimpse into the mind of a legendary RPG designer, resonating with players who value nuanced storytelling and the enduring appeal of player choice.

en.title: Fallout: New Vegas Director Reveals His 'Least Worst' Mojave Ending
en.summary: Josh Sawyer, the visionary director behind Fallout: New Vegas, has shared his personal ideal outcome for the Mojave Wasteland. Despite the game's multiple endings, Sawyer believes true 'optimal' satisfaction remains elusive in the harsh post-apocalyptic setting.
en.body:
The Mojave Wasteland in **Fallout: New Vegas** is a brutal, unforgiving place, and its endings reflect that grim reality. Players navigating the complex web of factions like Caesar's Legion, Mr. House, and the New California Republic often find themselves choosing the 'least worst' option, a sentiment echoed by the game's director, **Josh Sawyer**. In a recent interview on The Examined Game, Sawyer elaborated on his personal vision for an ideal, albeit imperfect, conclusion to the Courier's journey.

Sawyer expressed skepticism about handing the reins to any single dominant power. He views Caesar and Mr. House as inherently dangerous choices due to their singular vision and potential for unchecked control. The NCR, while perhaps possessing more noble intentions, is depicted with significant internal problems and questionable motivations, making them a difficult faction to fully endorse. Even the most virtuous individuals fighting for the NCR are caught within an imperialistic agenda that Sawyer finds hard to reconcile with a truly 'great' outcome.

## The Appeal of Independence

For **Josh Sawyer**, the most compelling ending is one where New Vegas achieves independence. This path, while fraught with its own set of challenges, represents a fresh start. Sawyer acknowledges that an independent Mojave would likely suffer from dysfunction, bureaucracy, and corruption. However, he emphasizes that this scenario has *not yet been tried* within the game's narrative. This element of the unknown, of forging a new path rather than succumbing to established or flawed powers, makes it his preferred, albeit imperfect, resolution for the Mojave Wasteland.

This perspective aligns with a significant portion of the **Fallout: New Vegas** player base, many of whom have long debated the merits and drawbacks of each faction's endgame. The game's enduring legacy is a testament to its complex moral landscape and the freedom it afforded players to shape the fate of the wasteland, even if that fate was never truly perfect.

## What's Next for Sawyer and Fallout?

While **Josh Sawyer** has spoken about his ideal **Fallout: New Vegas** ending, his current involvement with the franchise remains a topic of keen interest. Obsidian Entertainment, the studio he helms, has been confirmed to be working on new Fallout projects. Sawyer himself has been seen researching the Mojave and has praised the recent **Fallout** TV show as an "amazing adaptation." Specific details regarding any new games or their potential outcomes have not yet been announced.

tr.title: Fallout: New Vegas Yönetmeni Mojave'nin 'En Az Kötü' Sonunu Açıkladı
tr.summary: Fallout: New Vegas'in vizyoner yönetmeni Josh Sawyer, Mojave Çölü için kişisel ideal sonucunu paylaştı. Oyunun çoklu sonları olmasına rağmen Sawyer, gerçek 'optimal' doygunluğun zor post-apokaliptik ortamda elde edilmesi güç olduğunu düşünüyor. Sawyer, Mojave'nin geleceğini şekillendiren kararların hiçbirinin kolay olmadığına dikkat çekiyor.
tr.body:
Fallout: New Vegas'teki Mojave Çölü, bir o kadar acımasız ve bağışlayıcı olmayan bir yer. Oyuncular, Sezar'ın Lejyonu, Bay House ve Yeni Kaliforniya Cumhuriyeti gibi fraksiyonların karmaşık ağlarını navigasyon yaparken genellikle 'en az kötü' seçeneği seçiyorlar. Josh Sawyer da bu duyguyu paylaşıyor. The Examined Game'de yaptığı recent röportajda Sawyer, Courier'in yolculuğunun ideal, ancak mükemmel olmayan bir sonucunu paylaştı.

Sawyer, herhangi bir tek dominant güce hakimiyeti teslim etmek konusunda şüpheci. Sezar ve Bay House'u, tek bir vizyonları ve kontrol potansiyelleri nedeniyle tehlikeli seçenekler olarak görüyor. Yeni Kaliforniya Cumhuriyeti ise belki daha soylu niyetlere sahip, ancak önemli iç sorunlar ve şüpheli motivasyonlar nedeniyle tam olarak desteklenmesi zor bir fraksiyon. NCR için savaşan en erdemli bireyler bile, Sawyer'in gerçekten 'büyük' bir sonuçla uzlaşması zor olan emperyalist bir gündem içinde yer alıyor.

## Bağımsızlığın Çekiciliği

Josh Sawyer için en çekici son, New Vegas'in bağımsızlığını kazanması. Bu yol, kendi zorluklarına sahip olmakla birlikte, taze bir başlangıç temsil ediyor. Sawyer, bağımsız bir Mojave'nin muhtemelen disfonksiyon, bürokrasi ve yolsuzlukla karşı karşıya kalacağından bahsediyor. Ancak, oyunun anlatısında daha önce denenmemiş bir yolun ortaya çıkması, Sawyer'in tercih ettiği, ancak mükemmel olmayan bir çözüm olarak görüyor.

Bu perspektif, Fallout: New Vegas oyuncularının önemli bir bölümü ile uyumlu. Oyuncular, her fraksiyonun son oyununun artıları ve eksilerini uzun süredir tartışıyor. Oyunun kalıcı mirası, karmaşık ahlaki manzarası ve oyunculara çölün kaderini şekillendirmesi için verdiği özgürlüğe bir kanıttır, nawet bu kader asla mükemmel olmamıştır.

## Sawyer ve Fallout'un Geleceği

Josh Sawyer, ideal Fallout: New Vegas sonunu paylaştı, ancak franchise ile ilgili güncel katılımı hala büyük ilgi görüyor. Obsidian Entertainment stüdyosunda çalışıyor ve yeni Fallout projeleri üzerinde çalıştıkları onaylandı. Sawyer, Mojave hakkında araştırma yapıyor ve recent Fallout TV dizisini 'inanılmaz bir adaptasyon' olarak övdü. Yeni oyunlar veya olası sonuçlar hakkında específik detaylar henüz açıklanmadı.

content_raw: Fallout: New Vegas is a sprawling RPG filled with sketchy factions, greasy NPCs, rubbery morality, and tough decisions, all of which ultimately lead the player to one of four possible outcomes that share one thing in common: They're not great. Which isn't to say they're not satisfying, just that there's no optimal outcome where everybody's happy and nobody gets hurt. The wasteland is a pretty crappy place, after all, so outcomes tend to be crappy too. In a recent interview on The Examined Game with Steven Lake , New Vegas designer and director Josh Sawyer revealed his own personal 'best of a bad lot' pick for the endgame, and it's independence all the way. "It is very hard. I mean, some people would say like, I love Caesar, and great," Sawyer said. "But it's kind of hard to hand everything over to an individual like Caesar or Mr. House. It feels dangerous. And then with NCR, you just realize like, man, they got a lot of problems. Like, they have a lot of problems right now . They're doing things for a lot of very questionable reasons. "Even if you find people that you feel are very virtuous and and are sacrificing a lot to fight in the Mojave and not because they're trying to be imperialistic, even though NCR is being very imperialistic, it's difficult to wrestle with that and come away and say like, yeah, I think NCR is great." For Sawyer, then—and most players, apparently—an independent New Vegas is the least worst choice. "I know it's going to be dysfunctional, I know it's going to be bureaucratic, I know there's going to be corruption—but also it hasn't been tried yet, right? Like we haven't organized this yet, so let's give it a try." Sawyer said Obsidian tried to portray independence as having its own "drawbacks of dysfunction," arising from the proliferation of bureaucracy and the corruption that inevitably follows. Even so, I think I have to agree that it's probably the way to go: If there's one thing history keeps on trying to teach us, it's that handing the keys to an unstable autocrat or a fascist military superpower (or, god forbid, both at the same time) never goes well. For myself, I wrapped up Fallout: New Vegas with a fifth option that isn't canon, strictly speaking, but is my head canon: I got so sick of getting jerked around by the competing Mojave factions that when Mr. House asked me to take out the Brotherhood of Steel, I just packed up my stuff and wandered back out into the desert, never to return. Was I a little bored with Fallout: New Vegas at that point, after sinking countless dozens of hours into it? Sure. But turning my back on the grasping travails of the last ragged remnants of humanity and disappearing into swirling sand and crackling radiation, to be remembered only as that guy who did that stuff—that's real warrior of the wasteland stuff, baby. Sawyer, in case you hadn't heard, is reportedly heading up a new Fallout project at Obsidian , which would be nice except that it came amidst the recent major cuts at Xbox
